newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Bigmar sees FDA filings in 97.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Bigmar sees FDA filings in 97.

text.p: Bigmar Inc said on Thursday it will to begin filing generic drugs for approval with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in early 1997, latter adding proprietary drugs to the mix.

The company's initial focus will be on generic versions of widely available cancer drugs including doxorubicin, methotrexate and calcium leucovorin, Peter Stoelzle, Bigmar executive vice president, said in an interview.

Stoelzle, citing his past work directing pharmaceutical regulatory affairs at Bausch & Lomb Inc, said he thought Bigmar would be able to get generic drugs through the U.S. regulatory process in under 12 months, rather than the average time of around two years.
"Our expectation is that by the end of 1997 we will be able to see some positive results on the U.S. regulatory front," he said.
The drugs would be Columbus, Ohio-based Bigmar's first on the U.S. market.
It reported revenue for the first six months of 1996 of about $3.8 million, up from $1.7 million in 1995, mainly from sales of intravenous solutions and oncology drugs in Europe.
The company went public in June at 7-1/2 a share. It shares were off 3/8 at 6-1/2 on Thursday.

Stoelzle said the company's goal was to make one filing a month and eventually have 20 percent of the filings be for original drugs licensed from other sources including development partners or universities.
Bigmar has two manufacturing plants in Switzerland and acquiring or building a facility in the U.S. is "very much a part of our overall plan," Stoelzle said.
One of the first proprietary drugs the company is working on is a form of the blood-clot dissolver urokinase. A U.S. filing for the drug "is something we would like to happen in 1997," Stoelzle said.
Analysts estimate Abbott Laboratories Inc's urokinase drug, Abbokinase, will have 1996 sales of about $200 million.
